primitives.name: Kolmogorov Extension Theorem
primitives.verbatim_quote: Sur la loi forte des grandes nombres, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 191 (1930) 910–912.
primitives.latex: \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \; \exists \text{consistent probability measures } \mu_n \text{ on } \mathbb{R}^n \Rightarrow \exists \text{unique stochastic process } X: \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{T}}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Omega': 'Sample space (dimensionless)', 'X': 'Stochastic process (value space)', '\\mathbb{T}': 'Index set (dimensionless)', '\\mu_n': 'Finite-dimensional distribution (probability)', 'n': 'Dimension index (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Consistent finite-dimensional distributions across all time indices; complete probability space; separable state space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violations occur when marginal distributions fail to extend consistently to higher dimensions, leading to non-existent joint processes.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Prior specification for exchangeable sequences; GSE - State-transition kernel construction for Markov processes.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation of finite marginals against empirical data.

primitives.name: Loomis Abstract Congruence
primitives.verbatim_quote: Abstract congruence and the uniqueness of Haar measure, Ann. Math. 46 (1945) 348–355.
primitives.latex: G \text{ locally compact group}, \; \mu(A) = \mu(gA) \; \forall g \in G \Rightarrow \mu(B) = c \cdot \lambda(B) \; \forall Borel \; B \subseteq G
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G': 'Locally compact group (dimensionless)', '\\mu': 'Invariant measure (arbitrary units)', '\\lambda': 'Haar measure (same units as \\mu)', 'c': 'Normalizing constant (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Existence of a left-invariant regular Borel measure on the Borel sets of a locally compact topological group.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-uniqueness occurs when the group is not second-countable or when the measure fails to be regular, leading to multiple invariant extensions.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Invariant priors under symmetry transformations; GSE - Stationary state distributions in ergodic systems.
layer2.telemetry: Testing for scale invariance in empirical data via group actions.

primitives.name: Lévy Continued Fraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Théorie de l'addition des variables aléatoires, Paris, 1937.
primitives.latex: X_i \sim F \Rightarrow \lim_{n \to \infty} [a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n] = \frac{1}{a_1 + \frac{1}{a_2 + \ddots}} \text{ converges almost surely}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X_i': 'IID random variables (state space)', 'F': 'Common distribution (probability)', 'a_i': 'Continued fraction coefficients (dimensionless)', 'n': 'Number of terms (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Independent identically distributed entries with finite second moment; continued fraction representation exists.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Divergence happens when the variance becomes infinite, causing the limit to fail to exist or become degenerate.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Bayesian updating of stable laws; GSE - Recurrence relations in sequential decision trees.
layer2.telemetry: Monitoring continued fraction convergence as diagnostic for tail behavior.

Kolmogorov's theorem provides a rigorous existence proof for stochastic processes from consistent marginals, essential for both GSI's prior calibration and GSE's transition kernels. Loomis' abstract congruence establishes the uniqueness of Haar measure under group actions, directly informing invariant priors and stationary distributions. Finally, Lévy's continued fraction connects to stable distributions and recursive algorithms, relevant for sequential inference and state-space models. Their interplay reveals how abstract mathematical structures underpin practical computational frameworks while highlighting critical failure modes at singularities or non-ergodic limits.
